title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: It has been some time since I have had a letter from thee. I wrote to thee by post some time ago, and I don’t recollect anything that has transpired since that time that is worthwhile for me to inform thee of. I am in hopes that thee will receive this in Baltimore & if so, Brother & Sister will have the pleasure of informing thee how we are coming on here. David & Hannah Cattelll I expect will have the happiness of being at thy house. What a glorious thing it would be for me if I was ready to start on the same route that they propose taking, but alas! Such a pleasure is not for me to have yet a while. I am still in hopes that it will be for me sometime, but I have no idea when. Not until I get money plentier than I have at present. I have determined to sell my property in Ohio the first opportunity. It does not suit me to live there. Money is too scarce in that country for me, for I can’t pay my debts without it. I suppose that it would suit me if I was to do like Nathan has done, that is, take unto myself a wife, but I think that it is plenty time enough for me to do that. I am like old Eli Owman, I am not ready yet.

I have some prospect of teaching school this winter, either at Redstone or in this schoolhouse on the big run. The school master at Redstone is about to go away, & they have given me an invitation to succeed him, but whether it will be agreeable to all parties I don’t know. I shall know in the course of a few days, but I am a good deal afraid of it. Perhaps thee has not forgotten what sort of people live there, and that it has been impossible as yet for one to have them all pleased at once. I know that I have too many deficiencies to think of pleasing all. I have spent this season on the old home place at work for Elisha, but now he & his wife are gone & there is no other man or boy about the house (except Emmor). Mary’s sister Miriam, the black girl, and a small bound girl, with Elisha, little brother, constitute our family.

Little Emmor loves to divert and amuse me or else I should be much more tired of living so. He is just learning to talk and can holler Uncle, which is a new name for me. If he never has brothers or sisters he will certainly be a spoiled boy, for his father makes a great pet of him.

May we not anticipate the pleasure of seeing thee & father here before a great while. It is so late in the season now that I can’t reasonably look for you, I am in hopes that another season will not pass away without my seeing my endeared Mother.
I wrote to Sister Rachel by John Warrington, and I believe that I shall not write to her at this time.

I have been favored with health, which I esteem a blessing, except the toothache which I have been pestered with latterly. It has been about a year since I declined the filthy practice of chewing tobacco and I don’t think that I shall ever take to it again.
Accept the assurance of my love & affection. Give my love to father & Sister Rachel. I am with every sentiment of esteem and respect.
